question_title: Thunderbird keeps freezing after being left idle
question_content: Subject: Severe recurring UI freezes after upgrading Thunderbird from v114 to v150+ — application becomes unresponsive after being left idle**   Hello Thunderbird Support Team, I'm experiencing a serious and persistent performance issue with Thunderbird that began immediately after upgrading from version 114 to version 150 in September 2026. The problem has continued through multiple subsequent updates and is now severely affecting my daily work. I've been using Thunderbird for years, and it worked reliably before this major upgrade.  The problem**   Thunderbird launches normally and initially works perfectly. However, after I leave it open in the background while working in other applications, it frequently becomes completely unresponsive when I return to it. Specifically: - Thunderbird is initially fast and responsive after launching. - After approximately 5–10 minutes, or sometimes after a longer period of inactivity, it begins experiencing severe lag or freezes completely. - When I switch back to Thunderbird, the interface is often unresponsive for several minutes. - I often have to force-close the application through Windows because it becomes practically unusable. - Restarting Thunderbird temporarily restores normal performance, but the problem eventually returns, when it's left idle. - The issue occurs repeatedly throughout the day and makes it very difficult to use Thunderbird reliably. Importantly, this is not simply slow startup performance. Thunderbird initially works perfectly, and the freezing develops after it has been running for a while, particularly when left in the background.  Version and environment**   - Operating system: Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit - Thunderbird version before the upgrade: 114 - Version initially upgraded to: 150 - Subsequently confirmed version: 156.0.1 (64-bit), on September 29, 2026 - Problem first appeared: September 2026 - Problem still present: October 22, 2026 - Current Thunderbird version: 158.0.1  Troubleshooting already performed**   1. **Global search indexing:** I noticed that Thunderbird's Activity Manager frequently displayed "Indexing messages." I suspected that indexing might be causing the problem. 2. **Disabled Global Search and Indexer (Gloda):** Unfortunately, this made no meaningful difference. Thunderbird continued freezing even with global indexing disabled. 3. **Multiple Thunderbird updates:** The application has been updated repeatedly since the initial upgrade, but the freezing has persisted. 4. **Restarting Thunderbird:** Temporarily resolves the problem, but only until Thunderbird has been running for some time.  Additional unusual behavior: Google OAuth authentication**   On at least two occasions, after force-closing an unresponsive Thunderbird process, Google Chrome unexpectedly opened a Google authorization page saying: "Mozilla Thunderbird Email wants access to your Google Account." The page also indicated that Thunderbird already had some access to the Google account. After clicking "Continue," Chrome redirected to a localhost address (127.0.0.1 equivalent, using a dynamically assigned port), which failed with: "ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED — localhost refused to connect." I suspect this happens because Thunderbird is no longer running to receive the OAuth authorization callback. I'm not sure whether the Google authorization issue is directly related to the freezes, but the repeated timing is suspicious and could indicate a background synchronization or authentication problem.  Impact**   I use Thunderbird extensively for professional correspondence and managing my translation business. These recurring freezes are seriously disrupting my workflow. The problem has now persisted for over a month, despite updates and troubleshooting. It is becoming increasingly difficult to continue using Thunderbird in this condition.  What I would appreciate help investigating**   Could you please advise on how to identify the background process or operation that causes Thunderbird to become unresponsive after it has been running for several minutes? In particular, I would appreciate guidance on: - Whether this is a known regression affecting users who upgraded from much older Thunderbird versions. - Whether IMAP synchronization, background authentication, or Google OAuth activity could be responsible. - Whether there are diagnostic logs or performance profiles I can collect while Thunderbird is frozen. - Whether a particular database, profile component, or setting could be responsible without requiring me to rebuild my entire Thunderbird setup. - Whether there are known fixes or workarounds. I'm happy to provide additional diagnostic information, screenshots, or logs if that would help identify the cause. I would particularly appreciate a way to capture what Thunderbird is actually doing during these freezes, rather than continuing to try speculative troubleshooting steps. Thank you in advance for your assistance!

question_title: Outlook.de receives mail but cannot send with OAuth2: “SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox”
question_content: Hello, I cannot send email from my personal Outlook.de account in Thunderbird, although receiving email works. Sending email from the same account through Outlook.com in a web browser also works. This is a personal Microsoft account, not a business or school account. I do not have access to an Exchange Online or Microsoft 365 administration console. Environment: - Thunderbird version: 158.0.1 (the version reported when troubleshooting started) - Operating system: Windows 11 - Email provider: Outlook.com / Outlook.de Outgoing server settings: - Server: smtp-mail.outlook.com - Port: 587 - Connection security: STARTTLS - Authentication method: OAuth2 - Username: full Outlook.de email address OAuth2 was already configured before the problem was investigated. When I try to send an email, Thunderbird displays an authentication failure. A Microsoft sign-in page briefly opens and closes, after which the same error appears again. The Thunderbird Error Console reports: mailnews.smtp: Command failed: 535 Authentication unsuccessful, SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox. It also shows: currentAction=_actionAUTH_XOAUTH2 A second entry reports: mailnews.smtp: Authentication failed: Authentication unsuccessful, SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox. Troubleshooting already performed: 1. Verified the SMTP server, port, STARTTLS, OAuth2 and username. 2. Removed the saved Microsoft/Outlook authentication entries for this account. 3. Completely closed and restarted Thunderbird, then retried authentication and sending. 4. Checked the cookie exceptions list: no exceptions were present. 5. Confirmed that sending through Outlook.com in a browser works. Removing the saved authentication entries and signing in again did not resolve the issue. My questions: - Is this a known issue with personal Outlook.com/Outlook.de accounts? - Is there any supported Thunderbird-side fix for this specific server response? - Is a different supported account connection method available for this personal account that does not depend on SMTP AUTH? - If Microsoft must change something on the server side, what exactly should I ask Microsoft Support to investigate? I have found Microsoft's documentation about enabling SMTP AUTH in Exchange Online, but its administrator instructions do not apply to my personal Outlook.de account. I can provide a screenshot of the Thunderbird Error Console. Thank you for your help.

question_title: Yahoo-Mail lässt sich in Thunderbird 153.5 unter macOS nicht anmelden – „Es ist ein Problem aufgetreten“
question_content: Titel: Yahoo-Mail lässt sich in Thunderbird 153.5 unter macOS nicht anmelden – „Es ist ein Problem aufgetreten“**   Hallo zusammen, ich kann mein Yahoo-Mail-Konto seit etwa zwei Wochen nicht mehr in Thunderbird einrichten. Ich vermute ein Problem mit der Yahoo-OAuth2-Anmeldung.  Mein System:**   - Betriebssystem: macOS auf einem MacBook Pro - Thunderbird-Version: 153.5 - Weitere E-Mail-Konten in Thunderbird: Gmail, WEB.DE, GMX und Host Europe. Diese funktionieren alle problemlos.  Fehlerbeschreibung:**   Wenn ich mein Yahoo-Konto hinzufügen möchte, öffnet sich das Yahoo-Anmeldefenster. Ich gebe meine vollständige Yahoo-E-Mail-Adresse und mein korrektes Passwort ein. Anschließend erscheint folgende Fehlermeldung: „Es ist ein Problem aufgetreten. Wir konnten Sie nicht anmelden. Versuchen Sie es bitte auf einem anderen Gerät.“ Darunter befindet sich ein lila Button „Hilfe aufrufen“. Die Anmeldung bei Yahoo funktioniert dagegen problemlos über Firefox auf demselben Mac mit demselben Passwort. Auch die Anmeldung über meinen Passkey auf dem iPhone funktioniert.  Bereits durchgeführte Maßnahmen:**   - Yahoo-Passwort geändert und die Anmeldung über Firefox erfolgreich getestet. - Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung bei Yahoo aktiviert. - Yahoo-Konto in Thunderbird gelöscht und mehrfach versucht, es neu einzurichten. - Authentifizierungsmethode für IMAP und SMTP überprüft: OAuth2. - Cookies und JavaScript in Thunderbird aktiviert. - Im Konfigurationseditor folgende Werte überprüft:  - `mailnews.oauth.usePrivateBrowser = true`  - `mailnews.oauth.useExternalBrowser = false`  - `javascript.enabled = true`  - Ein Yahoo-App-Passwort erstellt und versucht, das Konto manuell mit „Passwort, normal“ einzurichten. Thunderbird öffnet trotzdem wieder das Yahoo-Anmeldefenster unter `autodiscover.yahoo.com`, wo dieselbe Fehlermeldung erscheint. - Alte Yahoo-Einträge aus dem Passwortspeicher entfernt. - Doppelte Yahoo-SMTP-Einträge gefunden und den veralteten Eintrag entfernt. - Thunderbird vollständig beendet und neu gestartet. Nach dem Neustart erscheint teilweise sogar eine Passwortabfrage für `peterbeck127@yahoo.com`, obwohl das Yahoo-Konto nicht mehr in der Kontenliste vorhanden ist.  Meine Fragen:**   1. Ist ein bekannter Fehler bei der Yahoo-OAuth2-/PKCE-Anmeldung in Thunderbird 153.5 vorhanden? 2. Warum lehnt Yahoo die Anmeldung in Thunderbird ab, obwohl dieselben Zugangsdaten über Firefox funktionieren? 3. Wie kann ich eventuell verbliebene Yahoo-Anmeldeversuche oder Servereinträge vollständig entfernen, ohne mein Thunderbird-Profil und meine anderen E-Mail-Konten zu beschädigen? 4. Gibt es einen bekannten Workaround oder eine Korrektur für dieses Problem? Ich möchte mein Yahoo-Konto wieder normal über IMAP und SMTP in Thunderbird verwenden können, ohne meine anderen Konten neu einrichten zu müssen. Vielen Dank für eure Hilfe!
